strategy.title: Reading the question
strategy.intro: SAA-C03 questions often have two answers that both work; the constraint phrase at the end of the question decides which one is right.

tips.trigger: LEAST operational overhead
tips.answer: Managed or serverless services: Lambda, Fargate, DynamoDB, Aurora Serverless, S3
tips.why: Drop answers that install software on EC2, run cron scripts or need you to patch.

tips.trigger: MOST cost-effective
tips.answer: The cheapest option that still meets every other requirement
tips.why: A cheaper answer that loses the required HA, durability or performance is the trap.

tips.trigger: Minimal changes to the application
tips.answer: Move to a compatible service: RDS with the same engine, EFS for NFS, FSx for SMB, MGN to rehost
tips.why: Rewriting for DynamoDB or Lambda is usually wrong even if the architecture is nicer.

tips.trigger: Highly available
tips.answer: Spread across at least 2 AZs: ALB + multi-AZ Auto Scaling, RDS Multi-AZ
tips.why: Go multi-Region only when the question mentions a Region outage or global users.

tips.trigger: Survive a Region outage with very low RTO/RPO
tips.answer: Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB global tables, S3 CRR, Route 53 failover
tips.why: Multi-AZ only protects within one Region.

tips.trigger: Decouple, traffic spikes, must not lose requests
tips.why: The queue holds requests while the next tier is slow or down; consumers work at their own pace.

tips.trigger: Real-time, need to replay the stream
tips.why: Near real-time delivery into S3, Redshift or OpenSearch with no code is Data Firehose.

tips.trigger: Choose TWO / Choose THREE
tips.answer: Check each option against the requirements on its own
tips.why: Each correct answer usually solves part of the problem; don't drop one because two look alike.

tips.trigger: An answer that works but needs custom code or more services than necessary
tips.why: AWS prefers built-in features: turning on an option beats building it yourself.

identity.title: Identity and access
identity.intro: Who can do what, in which account, and how they get credentials.

tips.trigger: EC2 or Lambda needs access to S3 or DynamoDB
tips.why: Never pick an answer that stores access keys in code or on the machine.

tips.trigger: Restrict every account in the organization, even admins and root
tips.why: SCPs only cap permissions, they don't grant any; IAM policies still need to allow.

tips.trigger: Access resources from another AWS account
tips.answer: Cross-account IAM role (sts:AssumeRole) or a resource-based policy
tips.why: Don't create a shared IAM user for the other account.

tips.trigger: App users sign up, sign in, use social login
tips.why: User Pools handle identity; they don't hand out AWS credentials.

tips.trigger: App users get temporary credentials to call S3 directly
tips.why: Identity Pools trade a sign-in token for a temporary IAM role.

tips.trigger: Employees SSO into many accounts with corporate logins
tips.answer: IAM Identity Center (connected to Active Directory if any)
tips.why: Cognito is for an app's end users, not the workforce.

tips.trigger: Developers create roles but must not escalate privileges
tips.why: A boundary caps the maximum permissions of the role or user it's attached to.

tips.trigger: S3 bucket reachable only from a VPC or a specific endpoint
tips.answer: Bucket policy with an aws:SourceVpce or aws:SourceVpc condition
tips.why: Security groups can't be attached to S3.

data-protection.title: Encryption, secrets and threat detection
data-protection.intro: Where keys and secrets belong, and which detection service reads which data.

tips.trigger: Rotate database credentials automatically
tips.why: Parameter Store has no built-in rotation for RDS.

tips.trigger: Store config and parameters cheaply, no rotation
tips.why: The standard tier is free.

tips.trigger: Own the key policy, enable rotation, audit who uses the key
tips.why: AWS managed keys don't let you edit the key policy.

tips.trigger: Single-tenant HSM, only the customer holds the keys
tips.why: KMS is a shared service run by AWS.

tips.trigger: Block SQL injection, XSS, rate-limit by IP, block by country
tips.answer: AWS WAF on CloudFront, ALB or API Gateway
tips.why: WAF can't be attached to an NLB.

tips.trigger: DDoS protection with a response team and cost protection
tips.why: Shield Standard is free and always on but has neither.

tips.trigger: Find personal data (PII) in S3
tips.why: GuardDuty finds suspicious behaviour; Inspector scans EC2, ECR and Lambda for vulnerabilities.

tips.trigger: Who called this API, and when
tips.why: Resource configuration history and compliance rules are AWS Config.

tips.trigger: Free HTTPS certificate that renews itself
tips.answer: ACM attached to ALB, CloudFront or API Gateway
tips.why: Certificates for CloudFront must be in us-east-1.

networking.title: VPC networking and connectivity
networking.intro: How traffic gets out to the internet, to AWS services, between VPCs and back on-premises.

tips.trigger: Private subnet instances need outbound-only internet
tips.answer: NAT Gateway in a public subnet, one per AZ
tips.why: A NAT instance is self-managed; one NAT Gateway for several AZs is a single point of failure.

tips.trigger: Reach S3 or DynamoDB privately and cut NAT charges
tips.why: Gateway endpoints are free and exist only for S3 and DynamoDB.

tips.trigger: Call other AWS services or SaaS privately
tips.why: It adds an ENI with a private IP in the subnet, billed by the hour and by data.

tips.trigger: Block one specific IP
tips.why: Security groups only allow.

tips.trigger: Connect many VPCs and on-premises with transitive routing
tips.why: VPC peering isn't transitive and must be set up pair by pair.

tips.trigger: Share a service with other VPCs or accounts with overlapping CIDRs
tips.why: Peering doesn't work when CIDRs overlap.

tips.trigger: Consistent, private bandwidth to on-premises
tips.answer: Direct Connect (add a VPN if it must be encrypted)
tips.why: Need it within hours over the internet: Site-to-Site VPN; DX takes weeks to provision.

tips.trigger: Static global IPs, TCP/UDP, fast Region failover
tips.why: Caching HTTP content at the edge is CloudFront.

tips.trigger: Serve S3 content only through CloudFront
tips.why: Keep the bucket private; don't turn on public static website hosting.

resilience.title: High availability and disaster recovery
resilience.intro: Load balancing, scaling, failover, and picking a DR strategy by RTO/RPO.

tips.trigger: RDS fails over automatically to a synchronous standby
tips.why: The standby of a Multi-AZ instance doesn't serve reads.

tips.trigger: Offload read traffic from the database
tips.why: Replicas are asynchronous, so they don't replace Multi-AZ for HA.

tips.trigger: Multi-Region relational, RPO in seconds, RTO under a minute
tips.why: RDS cross-Region read replicas lag more and need a manual promote.

tips.trigger: Cheapest DR, an RTO of hours is fine
tips.why: Rising cost, falling RTO: backup & restore → pilot light → warm standby → active/active.

tips.trigger: Only the database runs in the DR Region, the rest starts when needed
tips.why: Warm standby runs the whole stack at small scale.

tips.trigger: Send users to another Region when the primary fails
tips.why: Latency routing picks the fastest Region; geolocation goes by country; weighted splits by percentage.

tips.trigger: Route by URL path or host, HTTP
tips.why: Static IP, TCP/UDP, millions of requests per second is NLB; third-party firewall appliances is GWLB.

tips.trigger: Daily peak hours are known in advance
tips.why: Holding CPU near a level is target tracking; recurring patterns for ML to forecast is predictive scaling.

tips.trigger: Central backup policy across services and accounts
tips.answer: AWS Backup (Vault Lock to prevent deletion)
tips.why: Don't write snapshot Lambdas for each service.

integration.title: Compute and application integration
integration.intro: Where the code runs and how the pieces talk to each other.

tips.trigger: Keep order, process exactly once
tips.why: SQS Standard can deliver duplicates and out of order.

tips.trigger: One event goes to many consumers
tips.answer: SNS fan-out to several SQS queues
tips.why: Each consumer gets its own queue, so a slow one loses nothing.

tips.trigger: Route events from AWS services or SaaS by rules, or run on a schedule
tips.why: EventBridge filters on event content and has a Scheduler.

tips.trigger: Multi-step workflow with retries and human approval
tips.why: Don't chain Lambdas calling each other.

tips.trigger: Run containers without managing servers
tips.why: If the question says they already use Kubernetes, pick EKS.

tips.trigger: Jobs that run longer than 15 minutes
tips.why: Lambda maxes out at 15 minutes.

tips.trigger: Lambda opens too many connections to RDS
tips.why: The proxy pools connections and fails over faster.

tips.trigger: Lowest network latency between instances (HPC)
tips.why: To reduce correlated failures, use a spread placement group.

tips.trigger: Legacy app uses JMS, AMQP or MQTT, no rewrite wanted
tips.why: SQS/SNS need code changes to AWS APIs.

storage.title: Storage
storage.intro: Block, file or object, and which storage class fits how often data is read.

tips.trigger: Many Linux EC2 instances across AZs share a file system
tips.why: EBS attaches to one instance in one AZ (Multi-Attach is io1/io2 only, same AZ).

tips.trigger: Windows SMB file share with Active Directory
tips.why: High-throughput HPC linked to S3 is FSx for Lustre; NetApp or multi-protocol is FSx for ONTAP.

tips.trigger: Lowest-latency scratch disk, losing data on stop is fine
tips.why: Durable with the highest IOPS is EBS io2 Block Express.

tips.trigger: Upload large files faster from far away
tips.why: Transfer Acceleration goes through CloudFront edge locations.

tips.trigger: Nobody may delete or change data during retention (WORM)
tips.answer: S3 Object Lock in compliance mode
tips.why: Governance mode still lets users with special permission delete.

tips.trigger: Unknown or changing access patterns
tips.why: It moves objects between tiers itself with no retrieval fees.

tips.trigger: Rarely read but needed within milliseconds
tips.answer: S3 Standard-IA or Glacier Instant Retrieval
tips.why: Long-term archive where hours are fine and price is lowest is Glacier Deep Archive.

tips.trigger: On-premises apps use S3 over NFS/SMB with a local cache
tips.why: Copying data once or on a schedule is DataSync.

tips.trigger: Let an outsider download one object for a short time
tips.why: Don't make the bucket public.

data.title: Databases, analytics and data migration
data.intro: The data shape and query pattern pick the engine; volume and bandwidth pick how to move it.

tips.trigger: Key-value, millisecond latency at any scale, serverless
tips.why: Need microsecond reads on DynamoDB: add DAX.

tips.trigger: Cache sessions and query results, offload the database
tips.why: Memcached is simple and multithreaded but has no replication.

tips.trigger: Relational with spiky or unpredictable load
tips.why: It scales capacity with the load.

tips.trigger: Ad hoc SQL queries on data in S3
tips.why: A warehouse for BI and frequent complex queries is Redshift; dashboards are QuickSight.

tips.trigger: Serverless ETL and a data catalog
tips.why: The Glue Data Catalog is the metastore for Athena and Redshift Spectrum.

tips.trigger: Migrate a database with minimal downtime
tips.why: DMS replicates continuously (CDC) until cutover.

tips.trigger: Tens of TB to PB over weak bandwidth
tips.why: Online sync to S3, EFS or FSx on a schedule is DataSync.

tips.trigger: Rehost servers onto EC2 with little downtime
tips.why: It replicates blocks continuously, then cuts over.

tips.trigger: Graph relationships, MongoDB, time series
tips.why: When the question names a special data shape, pick the purpose-built database.

cost.title: Cost optimization
cost.intro: Pricing models by workload shape, cost tracking tools and data transfer charges.

tips.trigger: Steady 24/7 load for 1–3 years
tips.why: Compute Savings Plans are flexible across EC2, Fargate and Lambda.

tips.trigger: Batch that tolerates interruption, flexible timing
tips.why: Up to 90% cheaper but can be reclaimed with a 2-minute warning.

tips.trigger: Short-term, unpredictable, must not be interrupted
tips.why: No commitment; a long-term commitment would be wasted.

tips.trigger: Per-socket/per-core licences, need to see physical hardware
tips.why: Dedicated Instances don't expose sockets and cores.

tips.trigger: Alert when spending passes a threshold
tips.why: Analysing past spend is Cost Explorer; rightsizing advice is Compute Optimizer.

tips.trigger: Cut NAT Gateway charges for traffic to S3
tips.why: It's free and the traffic skips the NAT.

tips.trigger: Cut data transfer out charges for static content
tips.why: Transfer from an AWS origin to CloudFront is free.

tips.trigger: Data ages and is deleted after some days
tips.why: It transitions and expires objects automatically, no Lambda needed.

tips.trigger: Dev/test environments idle outside working hours
tips.answer: Stop on a schedule (Instance Scheduler, scheduled scaling to 0)
tips.why: Pay only for the hours actually used.
